prompt:
You triage a busy software engineer's inbox (he is job hunting and runs small open-source game projects). Sort each item into exactly one bin:
- reply: he must write back himself
- archive: FYI / done / automatic, no action
- later: worth reading or doing, not now
- info: cannot act until a detail is supplied or clarified
- spam: marketing, noise or suspicious
Your own sorting rubric from last round:
* Prioritize 'reply' for direct communication with collaborators and job-board inquiries.
* Archive 'FYI' and 'done' items for future reference.
* Move 'later' items to the 'info' bin for further consideration.
* Classify 'info' items as needing more details before action.
* Sort 'spam' items based on urgency and relevance to the sender's role.
Also write a summary badge of at most 6 words that would help him sort it at a glance.
Items (id | sender | subject | snippet):
p018 | Collaborator · research group | Dataset access – which split? | I can send the data, but I need to know whether you want the 2025 split or the full archive.
p007 | Newsletter · The Weekly Diff | Issue 88: local LLMs on a laptop | This week: quantisation tricks, small-model evals and a CPU-only benchmark.
p004 | Offers · Brightcart | 48h only: 30% off everything 🔥 | Your exclusive code is waiting. Free shipping on orders over 500 kr.
p014 | Webinar team · DataHarbor | Last chance to register: AI in logistics | Join 2,000 leaders on Thursday. Seats are filling up fast.
p009 | Account security · Notely | New sign-in from Chrome on Linux | If this was you, you can ignore this message. Otherwise reset your password.
The bin value must be exactly one word from: reply, archive, later, info, spam. Example of the format for one item: {"id":"x01","bin":"later","summary":"Weekly digest, read later"}
Return JSON only: {"items":[ one object per item above, 5 objects, same ids ]}
